topic: Course Overview, What is Calculus & Functions
core_points: Calculus comes from the Latin word for 'pebble' (ancient counting tool).
Calculus deals with dynamic change and motion, contrasting static algebra.
Real number line: continuous points from -∞ to +∞.
Functions: y = f(x) where x is input and y is output.

pillars.name: Differential Calculus
pillars.desc: Splitting quantities into infinitesimally small pieces to compute rates of change.

pillars.name: Integral Calculus
pillars.desc: Accumulating and summing small pieces to evaluate total areas and volumes.

practice_problems: Review real line intervals, domain, and range.

topic: Real Numbers, Intervals, Absolute Value & Inequalities
core_points: The Real Number System: Natural numbers, Integers, Rationals, and the continuous real line (-∞ to +∞)
Three Core Properties of R: Algebraic properties, Order properties, and the Completeness property
Intervals (Finite vs. Infinite): Open, closed, and half-open subsets across set notation, interval notation, and graphical representation
Absolute Value (|x|): Geometric interpretation as distance from the origin and piecewise algebraic definition
Inequality Rules: Preserving direction under addition/subtraction, reversing direction when multiplying/dividing by negatives, and solving linear inequalities
